title: Captured German SS documents at the National Archives
place_text: National Archives / Library of Congress, Washington DC

tellings.quote: archives, but I wanted to see the captured German documents from the war. They had this a bunch of microfilm.

plain: Microfilmed German documents seized after the Second World War, including papers of the SS, the Nazi elite guard led by Heinrich Himmler, sit in the National Archives in Washington, and the writer Peter Levenda says he went to read them. He tells it first-hand: "I wanted to see the captured German documents from the war. They had this a bunch of microfilm." It is where his research into the Nazi leadership's hidden interests started.
